text:
Alex: rolled continuous-batcher v2 to prod (small fleet) ~02:00 PT. wanted to call out an unexpected prefix-cache hit-rate drop on several endpoints.
Priya: saw it too — p50 token latency improved by ~12ms but cache hit-rate fell from 71% -> 46% on the search-query workload.
Sam: do we have cohort-wise breakdown? could be batch composition mixing prefixes.
Marta: yep, clicking into per-route metrics: for route /search: batch size median up 1.8x, queueing time up 6ms, but prefix-cache hits down 25pp.
Chen: quick hypothesis: continuous batching increases interleaving so batches contain more unique prefixes -> lower reuse of KV caches during same batch.
Elaine: exact. We saw similar when we increased max_wait_ms in the simulator last quarter. Batching is good for GPU throughput but harms prefix cache locality.
Alex: attaching profiler snapshot for the tail period (30m after roll). notable: kernel time per token down, but prefix-lookup and kv-decode stages increased CPU per request.
batcher-bot: perf-profile: summarize 30m window: p50 token latency 48ms -> 36ms (improved), p95 210ms -> 240ms (regressed), cache_hit_rate 71% -> 46%, avg_batch 6.2 -> 11.1.
Priya: p95 regression lines up with longer queueing for some requests that miss the cache and then end up doing full KV decode. We should be careful — it's not just throughput math.
Sam: can you paste the config we rolled? want to simulate locally.
Alex: here are key params we changed: ```
continuous_batching: enabled
max_wait_ms: 10  # (was 5)
min_batch_size: 2
cohort_rebalance: off
cohort_keying: default
```
Marta: cohort_rebalance off is the killer. previously we kept prefix-affinity for a short window which kept cache reuse high. v2 prioritized fill-rate over affinity.
Chen: options: lower max_wait_ms back to 5, re-enable cohort_rebalance, or add warmup prefetch for prefixes that are frequently seen in mixing batches.
Elaine: warmup prefetch would require predicting prefix set per tick; cheaper is to change keying so KV cache keys include short prefix fingerprint + session_id so the cache lookup can still hit even when interleaved? might increase cache size and memory pressure.
Priya: another experimental idea: when batcher notices high diversity (>X unique prefix buckets in window), temporarily switch to affinity mode for next N ticks to preserve hit-rate. dynamic fallback.
Sam: can we get an offline sim that replays real traffic and toggles these behaviors? I'll spin up the batcher-sim with the last 24h trace.
Alex: created a quick sim job: job id sim-171998-01. initial results show enabling cohort_rebalance recovers hit-rate to ~68% with only a 4% drop in overall tokens/sec.
Marta: good. what's the impact on p95 latencies?
Alex: p95 drops back to baseline ~215ms (from 240ms). tail improves.
Chen: potential longer term: make keying hierarchical: fast prefix fingerprint used for in-batch matching (small memory, high hit local), full prefix key for cross-batch persistent cache. That gives us best of both worlds but more complexity.
Elaine: also worth threading this into kernel-selection heuristics: when prefix hit-rate low, switch to smaller-kernel (lower mem) to reduce KV decode cost per miss. We have telemetry hooks for that.
Priya: action items: 1) Sam -> run sim toggles for cohort_rebalance and max_wait_ms (due EOD) 2) Alex/Marta -> prod config rollback plan if p95 stays >230ms after 2h 3) Chen -> prototype hierarchical keying doc (short note) 4) Elaine -> add rule in router to mark routes with high diversity so batcher can bias affinity.
Sam: on it. starting sim now, will share numbers in thread.
Alex: thanks. can everyone react with :eyes: when you read? will wait 30m before any automated rollback so oncall can decide.
Priya: :eyes:
Marta: :thumbsup:
Chen: :eyes:
Elaine: :eyes:
Sam: sim completed: cohort_rebalance on + max_wait_ms=7 gives hit-rate 64%, p50 token latency 38ms, p95 220ms, overall throughput -2.6%. posting full CSV to the perf channel.
Alex: great, let's iterate. if we can keep hit-rate >=60% with <5% throughput loss we'll prefer that.
Marta: I'll open a small runbook snippet for oncall to detect this class of regression: add a combined metric alert: (cache_hit_rate drop >10pp AND p95 increase >10%) -> page.
Priya: agreed. also add a synthetic perf test that pushes mixed-prefix traffic to catch this in pre-prod next time.
Chen: note: memory usage for KV cache increased ~12% when we tried hierarchical keying in sim; worth watching.
Alex: thanks team. moving to monitoring watch. will follow up with a rollout plan that toggles cohort_rebalance gradually across regions.
